=== file-001.md ===
# Homeward at Dusk

The streetlamps bloom as daylight thins,
Copper leaves skitter at my feet,
A chill slips softly through my sleeves,
While distant chimneys breathe their sweet.
I carry dusk along the lane,
With bread-warm windows in my sight,
The old gate leans, the hinges sigh,
And porch boards gather amber light.
Behind the door, the kettle sings,
My name seems waiting in the hall,
I set the long road from my shoulders,
And hear the quiet house recall.

=== file-001.md ===
Returning Home
The last gold leaves drift across the lane,
While dusk folds softly over field and stone.
I follow the lanterns through the cooling rain,
Their small lights calling me toward home.
The chimney smoke unthreads into the sky,
And crickets hush beneath the copper trees.
A familiar window gathers night nearby,
A kettle hums beyond the evening breeze.
My footsteps find the gate by memory,
The door opens with its quiet, amber glow.
Inside, the dark gives back a place for me,
And autumn settles gently, leaf by leaf, below.

=== file-001.md ===
The Way Home

Amber leaves hush beneath my feet,
The evening folds its violet light.
A chimney lifts a thread of smoke,
And swallows gather into night.
I turn where familiar windows gleam,
Past fences brushed with copper flame.
The key is warm within my hand;
The door remembers me by name.
Inside, the kettle starts to sing,
While dusk leans softly on the pane.
I set my wandering heart down slow,
And hear home breathing in the rain.

A copper hush lies folded on the lane;

I carry apples' sweetness on my sleeve,

The windows bloom; the dark begins to leave,
A kettle sings against the cooling night.
My steps grow softer on the familiar stone,
The porch remembers every coat and key.
I cross the threshold, no longer alone—
The autumn world settles quietly in me.

Autumn Homecoming

The last gold ember leans across the lane,
While dusk folds quiet valleys into blue.
I follow leaves that skitter in the rain,
Their amber whispers leading me to you.
Chimney smoke unthreads above the eaves,
A lantern opens softly by the door.
The wind lets go its handfuls from the trees,
And copper shadows settle on the floor.
I turn the latch; warm cinnamon and fire
Rise like a song I knew before my name.
Beyond, the moon ascends through branches bare,

The latch gives way; warm bread and shadows start—
